W2 (empirical), after E042. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 (E038) gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752. The 0.75 bar has about 0.2 pp of headroom. The 0.753 gate on seeds 0-2 is a coin flip for the tip itself.

Mechanisms, each tied to its experiments:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to about 30% at 20 px (E026, E033). E040 (40/0/30/30) cost 0.06 pp and missed the gate. E041 (12-step trim) cost 0.2 pp, so trimming the 28/32 px phases is costly.
4. Backward truncation on large maps was the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 (freeze at 60%) saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp. E039 (BN folding) lost 0.15 pp for about 0.03 s. E042 (conv1-only staggered freeze) read 0.7549 at 5.267 s, saving only about 0.05 s. The stem is nearly exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: truncation savings were larger than I modelled. Time-neutral accuracy gains were over-predicted. Accuracy fell whenever training signal was cut.

Unsure: whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge, and whether any trim can clear 0.753 on seeds 0-2. Systems changes (padding, profiling) have no direct measurement here.

forecasts.reason: Recalibration adds a small forward pass. Its effect is paired, but the final BN stats are probably near-fine already, so the gain is likely under 0.1 pp.
Smaller batches at 20 px are less efficient on the GPU and add steps. A gain of about 0.1 pp is plausible but within noise, and time rises about 3%.
Group 2 is the biggest block, but the freeze lasts only 10% of steps. It saves about 1.5% of time and probably costs 0.1-0.2 pp, in line with E037's cliff.
Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the tip is unchanged and bit-identical. The trace will most likely show the stem inefficient, since E028 saved more than its FLOP share.
E031 gave about 2.3 s/pp. A 95% keep saves about 3% of time for about 0.12 pp, which cannot be resolved against the noise.
Math is identical, so accuracy is noise-level. The saving is plausible at 1-2% if Cin=24 is slow, though cuDNN may already pad internally. Reshuffled kernels change the numerics slightly.

cruxes: Does the profiler show group-1 conv1 (Cin=24) running at low tensor-core efficiency? If so, I073 is a free win of about 2%. If not, the stem is exhausted.
What is the accuracy-per-second exchange rate of the remaining trims, as measured on unselected seeds 13-32? If every trim costs more than about 1.5 s/pp, the tip is at the Pareto front.
Is the population mean (about 0.752) enough for the 40-seed judge at 0.75? Any further cut needs a paired, unselected check.
